info.bio:
This Mortal Coil fue un proyecto de Ivo Watts-Russell, presidente de la compañía discográfica inglesa 4AD, que comenzó en 1983 y acabó en 1991. Se trataba de una seleción de miembros de diferentes bandas del sello que conformaban un nuevo supergrupo.

La banda toma su nombre de Shakespeare. En particular del soliloquio de Hamlet: "Ser o no ser", donde hace referencia a la muerte; "coil" es usado en un sentido arcaico como sinónimo de "problema".

podcast.title: Dreampop Supergroup
podcast.body: This Mortal Coil was a significant band of its era, often described as a "Dreampop Supergroup." It featured Ivo Watts-Russell, the founder of 4AD, along with members of Cocteau Twins and Dead Can Dance.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sampled by Nine Inch Nails
podcast.body: Samples from This Mortal Coil were incorporated into Nine Inch Nails' first album, "Pretty Hate Machine." These were heavily modified and mutilated by computers by Chris Vrenna, making their origins obscure in the final mix. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Failed Song Licensing for "Blue Velvet"
xref.body: For his 1986 film "Blue Velvet," Lynch attempted to license "Song to the Siren" by This Mortal Coil from 4AD, but the label refused. This led him to collaborate with Angelo Badalamenti and Julee Cruise for the film's soundtrack.

xref.title: Sampled by Nine Inch Nails
xref.body: Audio samples from Jane's Addiction were utilized on Nine Inch Nails' debut album, "Pretty Hate Machine." These samples were heavily processed and often made unrecognizable through computer modification by Chris Vrenna. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

Chris Vrenna manipulated these samples with computers, rendering them largely unidentifiable within the album's tracks. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

xref.title: Sampling on Pretty Hate Machine
xref.body: The debut album "Pretty Hate Machine" extensively utilized samples from various artists, including Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, and This Mortal Coil. These samples were often heavily modified and mutilated by computers, making them largely unrecognizable in the final tracks, a technique Chris Vrenna was particularly skilled at. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."
